nodes.label: MINDRAIL PROTOCOL Managed Section
nodes.rationale: The section mirrors specification 117 verbatim so the agent-facing protocol has a single source and is delimited by BEGIN/END markers that must not be hand-edited.

nodes.label: MCP Parameter Surface
nodes.rationale: All 13 tools ship in 0.1; only the parameter surface is constrained, because adding a field later is backward compatible while changing or removing a published one is not.

nodes.label: Protocol Skipped Scenario
nodes.rationale: The protocol-skipped scenario is mandatory because a suite that only exercises the protocol-compliant path would never catch a registered-only attribution engine.

nodes.label: Managed Section Tool Coverage
nodes.rationale: The managed section must cover all 13 tools: dropping a tool from the protocol presented to the agent means that tool is never called in practice.

nodes.label: Session Correctness Path
nodes.rationale: Spec 99 states the happy path and the correctness path are not two implementations; after_change, complete and verify all call the same reconcile engine, before_change only supplies a better baseline and lease context.

nodes.label: Not Yet Active Status Note
nodes.rationale: The block states the mindrail_* tools do not exist yet and calling them will fail; mindrail init will own and rewrite the section once the binary ships.

nodes.label: Exit Condition
nodes.rationale: 0.1 is complete when an agent cannot bypass the gate by forgetting a protocol call, skipping the local hook, renaming a protected symbol, weakening its critical test or claiming stale results as proof.

nodes.label: Reconcile Implementation Rule
nodes.rationale: Reconcile is the canonical change-discovery path, not an exceptional recovery utility; there must be one attribution engine rather than separate registered and unregistered implementations.

nodes.label: Reconcile In Fifth Milestone
nodes.rationale: Reconcile lands with the change engine, not after it: shipping before_change/after_change first and adding reconcile later guarantees the second attribution engine that section 61 forbids.

nodes.label: Reconcile Workflow
nodes.rationale: before_change improves coordination; reconcile provides correctness, so Mindrail never depends on the agent following the protocol 100%.

nodes.label: Resolver Pool Eviction
nodes.rationale: The pool key does not merge across worktrees, so process count grows with workspaces x project units; a fixed small ceiling causes evict/restart thrash and resolver cold start costs seconds.

nodes.label: Structural Precision Limits
nodes.rationale: 0.1 has no semantic resolver, so name-and-scope reverse lookup would produce over-broad impact sets; capping structural edge confidence at 0.5 and reverse depth at 1 keeps conservative validation from degenerating into running the whole suite on every edit.

nodes.label: Impact Fanout
nodes.rationale: Aggregation is a presentation boundary, not an analysis boundary: the full impact stays in the DB while MCP context is summarized.

nodes.label: Uncertainty Increases Evidence
nodes.rationale: Low confidence must not fail open or fail closed automatically; uncertainty raises the amount of required proof instead.

nodes.label: No Global Write Broker
nodes.rationale: Target is a few local concurrent agents; a global broker/daemon adds IPC, lifecycle and recovery complexity, so contention is measured before such an architecture is considered.

nodes.label: Mindrail Technology Stack and Implementation Guide
nodes.norm_label: mindrail technology stack and implementation guide

nodes.label: SQLite Driver Policy
nodes.rationale: Mindrail already needs a native C toolchain for the Tree-sitter binding, so avoiding CGO is not by itself a reason to pick a driver; the choice is benchmark-gated behind ADR-0002.

nodes.label: Subordinate To Spec
nodes.rationale: If an implementation choice conflicts with Technical Specification 1.0, the specification wins; this document must not redefine task, lease, invariant, impact, evidence or completion semantics.

nodes.label: Milestone Mapping Table
nodes.rationale: The seven build-order milestones are not a competing plan; where they differ from specification 128, the specification wins on scope and this document wins on sequencing.

nodes.label: Schema Policy v1
nodes.rationale: schema_version and the fail-closed branch ship in 0.1 even though the mixed-version reader window is deferred, because retrofitting them later would require rewriting existing repository knowledge.

nodes.label: Repository Layout
nodes.rationale: Spec 8 deliberately removed a separate .mindrail/protocol.md; the agent protocol lives in the AGENTS.md managed section so it sits in a file the agent already reads and has a single source.

nodes.label: CI In Scope Rationale
nodes.rationale: A pre-commit hook alone is not a gate because git commit --no-verify bypasses it entirely and agents genuinely reach for that flag, so verify --ci is in scope for 0.1.

nodes.label: System Git Adapter
nodes.rationale: System Git already defines exact index, worktree, merge-base, rename and porcelain behavior, so the Git executable is the more faithful implementation than go-git.

nodes.label: Soft vs Hard Enforcement
nodes.rationale: AGENTS.md, MCP next_actions and warnings are soft; leases, the completion gate, pre-commit, CI verify and critical evidence policy are the hard gates.

nodes.label: Soft Enforcement Note
nodes.rationale: The managed section is soft enforcement per specification 118: skipping a protocol call does not bypass the gate because reconcile discovers the actual diff from Git regardless.
